data.answer: This query identifies the single test file that links to the greatest number of distinct source files. It joins the test-link associations to the file inventory so that only files flagged as tests are considered as the linking side, then groups the links by test file path and counts the distinct target files each one references. Results are ordered by that distinct target count from highest to lowest, with ties broken alphabetically by the test file path, and only the top row is returned.

display_annotations.note: Deterministic display links; not source citations made by the model.

output_contract.guidance: Return both the test file path and its distinct target count. Break ties by test_file_id ascending.

data.question: Which test file links to the most source files?
data.reference_sql:
SELECT test_file_id, COUNT(DISTINCT target_file_id) AS targets
FROM code.test_links
GROUP BY test_file_id
ORDER BY targets DESC, test_file_id
LIMIT 1;

request.evidence: Count distinct target files per test file; ties are broken by path.
request.question:
Which test file links to the most source files?

Requested output columns: test_file_id (string), targets (integer).
Return every requested field using exactly its specified column alias. Preserve complete case-sensitive repository-relative paths and symbol IDs; do not substitute display names. Include all requested counts and provenance fields. Explain the query result in ordinary prose; do not emit placeholder text. These questions concern a static map of open-source Python code. Describe what the query computes and the assumptions it makes; the returned rows are reported separately. Questions asking which files, modules or symbols mean distinct identities, not one repeated row per matching import or call occurrence; preserve occurrence counts only when requested. Caller/callee graph questions include methods as well as standalone functions unless a symbol kind is explicitly restricted. Use files.is_test for test-file classification; test_links describe associations, not the complete set of test files. Use DOUBLE or DECIMAL, rather than single-precision REAL, for percentage calculations.
Return both the test file path and its distinct target count. Break ties by test_file_id ascending.

data.sql: SELECT tl.test_file_id, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT tl.target_file_id) AS INTEGER) AS targets FROM code.test_links AS tl JOIN code.files AS f ON tl.test_file_id = f.file_id WHERE f.is_test = TRUE GROUP BY tl.test_file_id ORDER BY targets DESC, tl.test_file_id ASC LIMIT 1
